plan.title: Liver treated vs control DE (n=3/3) with power caveats
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is 12,000 x 7 raw gene-level Salmon counts for human liver, 3 treated vs 3 control (one column is presumably a gene-symbol column, leaving 6 samples matching the 6x2 metadata table), single batch, unpaired. The gene-level counts (already aggregated from Salmon, no separate transcript-level quant.sf/tximport object available) go directly into DESeq2: QC first (blind VST, PCA, sample-distance heatmap, library sizes) to confirm the 3 vs 3 split before any modelling, then a minimal count filter, median-of-ratios normalization internal to DESeq2, an explicit-reference-level design, a Wald test with apeglm shrinkage, BH-adjusted results at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering, and an edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test on the same filtered counts/design as a robustness cross-check (rule R-0042: report the intersection as the high-confidence set). Because the smallest group holds only 3 replicates, the knowledge base's R-0017/R-0094 flags apply directly: power is low, only large-effect genes are reliably detected, and the report must state this explicitly rather than loosening thresholds to compensate. A ranked fgsea GSEA on the Wald statistic follows against the MSigDB Hallmark set (staged locally), with Reactome as the stated second-pass collection (also staged locally) for genes with signal too diffuse to survive per-gene FDR. The final report step consolidates DE tables, fit diagnostics (MA plot, dispersion plot), the DESeq2/edgeR overlap, the GSEA leading-edge genes, and an explicit power/reproducibility statement — no translational/biomarker steps are added since the research question asks only about DE and confidence at n=3, not clinical outcome or drug-target follow-up.
